blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Analyzes a project repository to understand its stack, architecture, and conventions. Creates missing documentation in .maestro/docs/. Produces structured project context for downstream agents.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Decomposes a development task into atomic, dependency-ordered implementation steps. Reads project files to understand structure before planning.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Implements a single step from a development plan. Uses an agentic loop to read context files, write code, and verify it compiles. Receives exactly one step at a time via the for-each loop in the workflow.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Detects the test framework, runs tests, parses results, and optionally runs type checking. Handles vitest, jest, mocha, pytest, cargo test.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Reviews code changes against conventions and test results. Produces a structured review with score, approval status, per-axis ratings, and actionable issues. Single LLM call — no agentic loop.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Creates a clean git commit for implemented changes. Runs git status/diff, generates a conventional commit message, selectively stages files, and commits.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Validates that an implementation step was completed by checking the filesystem. Returns specific errors if files are missing or empty.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Generic JSON validator. Schema is passed as input (not hardcoded). Strips prefixes, extracts from markdown, validates required fields/types/allowed values. Returns cleaned JSON or specific error messages.

blocks.author: cli-user
blocks.description: Complete autonomous development workflow v3: analyze → validate → plan → validate → for-each step (implement + verify) → test → review → commit. Uses json-validator and step-validator blocks for anti-hallucination.
